To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

patients with macroscopically multifocal breast cancers have an increased local recurrence rate, especially if multipicity is clinically apparent or when three or more gross tumors are identified on gross pathologic exam.
patients who present with multiple tumors in the breast are at increased risk for local recurrence, especially if the tumors are clinically evident.
macroscopic multifocality in breast cancer is associated with increased local recurrence rates.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the molecular biology of breast cancer.
the treatment of macroscopically multicentric cancers, and we have found that the risk of local recurrence is significantly increased in this subset of breast cancers.
the development of new and more effective treatments for breast cancer, with particular attention to the role of radiotherapy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

patients with multiple breast cancers have a higher risk of local recurrence and should be treated with a higher radiation dose and/or a more extensive surgery than patients with single breast cancers.
patients with multiple breast cancers have a higher risk of local recurrence and that the risk increases as the number of foci increases.
breast cancer patients with macroscopically evident multifocality are at high risk for local recurrence and should be considered for mastectomy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the presence of multiple foci of tumor in the breast is an important prognostic factor, and that the presence of clinically apparent multiple tumors, or of three or more grossly apparent tumor foci, is associated with a high risk of local failure.
breast‐conserving therapy for macroscopically multifocal breast cancers should not be discouraged.

the local failure risk for patients with multiple breast cancers is higher than that of patients with single lesions, and that local failure in these patients is more likely to be diffuse, multifocal, or associated with skin involvement.
The main takeaway from our work is that
breast cancers with grossly evident multifocal involvement have a higher risk of failure than those with a single focus of cancer.
patients with multiple cancers have an increased risk of local failure.

the presence of multiple foci in breast cancer is an important prognostic factor, and it is important to recognize it and to take into account the possibility of multiple foci when planning the management of breast cancer patients.
